name: Physiotherapy and rehabilitation

problems.words: Patients buy ten sessions, come for four and stop
quick_ideas: List current packages with sessions left and last visit date, so drop-offs are visible
Call those who missed two booked sessions, with their permission, so they hear from you early.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — a package tracker that alerts the front desk when someone misses sessions and sends a rebooking prompt with no health details, tracking completion by therapist.

problems.ask_first: How do you track sessions left today?
problems.free_stops: Alert rules and follow-up steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare open packages by start month and latest visit, so you see which buying periods stop showing up sooner.
Give one person a weekly notebook list of package holders with long gaps, so follow-up stops getting missed at the desk.

problems.words: Unused package sessions sit on the books and I don't know what I owe
quick_ideas: Total unused sessions across open packages, so the liability is known
Write down your package expiry policy, so staff answer consistently.

workzap_build.text: a package ledger showing sessions bought, used, remaining and expiry, with outstanding value updated daily.

problems.ask_first: Do your packages have an expiry date now?
problems.free_stops: Ledger structure and expiry handling are in the solution document; talk to your accountant on how to record it.

extra_ideas.text: Compare package sales notes with attended visit notes for open packages, so what may still be owed is easier to spot.
Keep one notebook page for every open package balance, so refund questions are answered from one place.

problems.words: Therapists' diaries have big gaps in the middle of the day
quick_ideas: Map one week of bookings per therapist by hour, so gaps are clear
Offer midday slots to flexible patients first, so peak hours ease.

workzap_build.text: therapist-wise WhatsApp booking with reminders and easy rescheduling, with utilisation measured per therapist.

problems.ask_first: Which hours stay empty most often?
problems.free_stops: Slot rules are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each therapist's midday gaps across this week, so you can see whose book is hardest to fill.
Give the front desk one midday openings list to check at booking time, so quieter hours get offered more consistently.

problems.words: Home-visit therapists say they went but I can't confirm
quick_ideas: Ask home-visit therapists to message on arrival and leaving, so visits are on record
Cross-check a few visits with the patient side, with permission, so you know the gap.

workzap_build.text: a home-visit planner with check-in and check-out by location and visit confirmation, with weekly completed-visit totals.

problems.ask_first: How many therapists do home visits?
problems.free_stops: Check-in rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note planned home visits beside therapist return times for this week, so you can compare field time with the route claimed.
Give one coordinator the daily home-visit notebook, so departures and returns are checked from one place.

problems.words: Per-session therapists dispute how many sessions they did
quick_ideas: Share this week's session count with each therapist, so differences surface early
Agree one record both sides accept, so there is one count.

workzap_build.text: a session log feeding a monthly pay statement for per-session staff.

problems.ask_first: Are therapists paid per session or salaried?
problems.free_stops: Pay rules and statement format are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare diary bookings with end-of-day attendance marks for each therapist this week, so count differences show before pay talk starts.
Assign one person to close each therapist's daily count in one notebook, so disputes have a single agreed source.

problems.words: Direct-billed claims take months to pay
quick_ideas: List open claims by reference, insurer and date sent, so ageing is visible
Note rejection reasons, so repeat paperwork gaps are fixed.

workzap_build.text: workflow_automation — a claims tracker with a document checklist per claim type, submission dates, rejections and payments by insurer.

problems.ask_first: Which insurers or claim types cause the most rejections?
problems.free_stops: Checklists per claim type are in the solution document; insurer rules are for your adviser.

extra_ideas.text: Compare claim send dates by payer and by clinic location, so you can spot where the longest waits keep clustering.
Give one staff member a fixed weekly claim-check hour, so unpaid files are reviewed before they drift further.

problems.words: Front desk forgets to collect the co-pay
quick_ideas: Check one week of visits against co-pays collected, so missed amounts show
Add co-pay to the checkout step, so it isn't left to memory.

workzap_build.text: a daily close matching sessions delivered against co-pays and payments, flagging misses.

problems.ask_first: Do most patients pay a co-pay or the full fee?
problems.free_stops: The close format is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare front-desk collection notes with the day's attended visits, so you see which shifts miss co-pay collection most often.
Make one person sign off the co-pay list before the desk closes, so unpaid visits are chased the same day.

problems.words: Surgeons who used to send patients have gone quiet
quick_ideas: List referral sources with monthly numbers, so drops are visible
Visit the ones that slowed, so you hear why.

workzap_build.text: a referral tracker with monthly volume per referring practice, flagging drops.

problems.ask_first: Is the referral source recorded at booking?
problems.free_stops: How referrals are captured is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare recent referral slips or notes with the same period earlier, so the quiet sources stand out by name.
Give one person a weekly walk-round list of quiet referral sources, so outreach keeps happening without waiting for the owner.

problems.words: Enquiries on WhatsApp aren't followed up
quick_ideas: Go through last week's enquiries and see how many got a reply, so the gap is measured
Give one person fixed reply times, so enquiries have an owner.

workzap_build.text: one inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram and Google enquiries with response timers and follow-up reminders.

problems.free_stops: Routing set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count unanswered enquiry chats at the same time each day this week, so the slow periods become visible.
Give one staff member one notebook page for new enquiries each shift, so every chat has a clear follow-up owner.

problems.words: Session reminders are sent manually one by one
quick_ideas: Count how long reminders take each day, so the cost is known
Ask patients at booking if they want reminders, so permission is in place.

workzap_build.text: reminders sent for every booked session, with time and place only, to consenting patients.

problems.ask_first: What do you use for bookings today?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many reminder messages each staff member sends before closing this week, so you see where the manual load really sits.
Give one staff member the reminder list for each next day, so missed bookings are less likely at opening time.

never_say: Exercises, treatments, session counts or return-to-work or sport timing.
Whether a treatment is working or an injury is healing.
Interpretations of WSIB, motor-accident or insurer rules.
Help billing for sessions not delivered or inflating session counts.
Ideas that put injuries or progress notes in messages.
Promises that packages will be completed more often.

sample_reply.person: Most of our patients buy a 10-session package and vanish after 4 or 5. Any way to fix this?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be brought under control, and none of it needs special equipment.
First, list current packages with sessions left and last visit date, so you can see who has dropped off.
Second, call anyone who has missed two booked sessions, with their permission, so they hear from you before they drift away.
A lasting version would be: with a package tracker that alerts the front desk and sends rebooking prompts, measured by therapist.

Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
